title: Presence cache future ts never ages and bypasses purge
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/presence.py PresenceCacheResource.record / snapshot / purge_older_than

record() stores caller ts after _finite_non_negative only (any finite ts >= 0). snapshot() computes age_s via age_s_at, which clamps negative deltas to 0. purge_older_than removes entries with ts < cutoff.

A recorded ts in the future therefore:
- Advertises age_s=0 on every GET/Observe until wall time catches up.
- Survives purge_older_than(now - TTL), because future ts is not less than the cutoff.

Spec 18.5.2 cache is a table of recently-heard peers. Overheard or spoofed presence with a far-future ts stays "fresh" forever. Distinct from open k208 (unbounded table / unused TTL hook): even a correct TTL cutoff cannot evict future-dated rows.

record() is the ingest path for peer documents; ts is not capped to now or to uint64.
acceptance_criteria: record() does not leave entries that report age_s=0 and survive a now-based TTL purge because ts is in the future. GET age_s reflects time since last hear, and purge_older_than(now - max_age) removes them. Tests cover ts > now.
